header.title: Low stock correlation makes sector and thematic selection the key diversifier within equities

s01_bottom_line.text: The Cboe 3-month implied correlation index sits at 11.2 versus a long-run average of 41, and only ~43% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day average (down from 75% in mid-August), indicating unusually low correlation and narrow breadth. ⟨cited figures: approximate; approximate, read from a chart⟩

The article states low correlation offers an opportunity to diversify risk within the equities market at both a sector and thematic level, and that dispersion may become one of investors' most valuable tools.

With bonds offering weaker diversification amid a positive stock-bond correlation, the article argues the diversification opportunity has shifted inside equities, raising the payoff to sector and thematic stock selection rather than index exposure.
